hints: Focus on what stays the same in a reduction, the carbon skeleton never changes, only the functional groups do.
Draw out 4-methylpentane-2,3-diol and notice you need OH groups on C2 and C3 of a 5-carbon chain with a methyl branch on C4.
Remember that LiAlH4 turns each aldehyde into a primary alcohol and each ketone into a secondary alcohol, so work backwards to see which two C=O groups could give those two CH-OH groups.
walkthrough:
**Draw the product skeleton**

Think of the name as instructions for the carbon backbone. 4-methylpentane-2,3-diol means a 5-carbon chain, OH groups on C2 and C3, and a methyl branch on C4.

Product skeleton:
$$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH(OH)}-\text{CH(OH)}-\text{CH(CH}_3)-\text{CH}_3$$

**Recall what LiAlH4 does**

LiAlH4 is a strong reducing agent. It adds hydride to carbonyls but does not change C-C bonds.

Key rule:
$$\text{R-CHO} \xrightarrow{\text{LiAlH}_4} \text{R-CH}_2\text{OH}$$
$$\text{R-CO-R'} \xrightarrow{\text{LiAlH}_4} \text{R-CH(OH)-R'}$$

**Work backwards from diol to dicarbonyl**

Both C2 and C3 in the product are CH(OH) groups, so both are secondary alcohols. That means both must have come from ketones, not aldehydes.

So R must be:
$$\text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-\text{CO}-\text{CH(CH}_3)-\text{CH}_3$$
This is 4-methylpentane-2,3-dione.

**Match to the options**

Only one structure has a 5-carbon main chain, a methyl on C4, and two ketone C=O groups exactly on C2 and C3. That structure reduces cleanly to 4-methylpentane-2,3-diol.

options.A: Correct. This is CH3-CO-CO-CH(CH3)2, which is 4-methylpentane-2,3-dione. Reduction of the two ketones at C2 and C3 gives CH3-CH(OH)-CH(OH)-CH(CH3)2, exactly 4-methylpentane-2,3-diol. Carbon skeleton and positions match perfectly.
options.B: Incorrect. This has an aldehyde at C1 and a ketone at C2. LiAlH4 would give a primary alcohol at C1 and a secondary alcohol at C2, forming a 1,2-diol, not a 2,3-diol. The trap is seeing two C=O groups and ignoring aldehyde versus ketone position.
options.C: Incorrect. This is 3-methylpentane-2,4-dione. Reduction would give OH groups on C2 and C4, forming 3-methylpentane-2,4-diol. The trap is miscounting the carbon chain and thinking any branched diketone will work.
options.D: Incorrect. This has an aldehyde at C1 and a ketone at C3. Reduction would give HOCH2-CH(CH3)-CH(OH)-CH2-CH3, a 1,3-diol with the methyl on C2. The trap is not checking both the diol positions and the methyl branch position.
